subject: Communication
title: Internal vs. External Self-Awareness
description: A fast breakdown of Internal vs. External Self-Awareness for builders.

hook.text: He knew exactly what he felt and why. But he had no idea how others experienced him. Half-aware is half-blind.

buildup.text: Tasha Eurich distinguishes two types: internal self-awareness (knowing your emotions) and external (how others see you).

discovery.text: They're independent. You can be high on one and low on the other. True self-awareness requires both.

twist.text: Introspection alone doesn't improve self-awareness. In fact, excessive 'why' questioning can create false narratives.

climax.text: Eurich found that 'what' questions ('What am I feeling?') beat 'why' questions — 'why' traps us in ruminative loops.

punchline.text: Don't just look inward. Learn how you land outward.

quiz.question: Which type of question improves self-awareness more, according to Eurich?

details.summary: Internal self-awareness means understanding your own emotions, values, and patterns. External self-awareness means understanding how others perceive you. Research by Tasha Eurich shows the two are independent: most people are high on one but not both.
details.whyItMatters: You need both types of self-awareness for effective communication. Being blind to either creates interpersonal problems you cannot see.
takeaways: Internal: understanding your own emotions and patterns
External: understanding how others perceive you
The two are independent and both must be developed

faq.question: How do you develop external self-awareness?
faq.answer: Seek honest feedback from people who will tell you the truth. Ask specific questions like 'What is one thing I do that undermines my message?' rather than vague ones like 'How am I doing?' Create psychological safety for honest responses and listen without defending.

faq.question: Why are the two types of self-awareness independent?
faq.answer: Introspective people may understand themselves deeply but be oblivious to how they come across. Socially attuned people may read others expertly but never examine their own patterns. Different skills and habits develop each type.
